output.sql:
WITH gaps AS (
  SELECT o.order_date - LAG(o.order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY o.customer_id ORDER BY o.order_date, o.order_id) AS days_between
  FROM marts.fct_orders AS o
  JOIN marts.dim_customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE o.is_revenue AND c.segment = 'enterprise'
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(days_between), 2) AS avg_days_between_orders
FROM gaps
WHERE days_between IS NOT NULL
output.explanation: For each enterprise customer, completed orders are sorted by date and the days since the previous completed order are calculated. The result averages all these gaps together, so customers with more orders carry more weight. It is not an average of per-customer averages. Two orders on the same day count as a 0-day gap, and customers with only one completed order contribute nothing.
